headline: CBA's cash NPAT increased $730 million or 7% to $10,982 million in FY26 (statutory: $10,866 million). Total operating income grew $1,759 million to $30,224 million, driven by a $1,563 million increase in NII and $196 million in other operating income. Operating performance rose $1,000 million to $16,469 million, despite underlying operating expenses increasing $719 million and notable items rising $40 million. Loan impairment expense increased $62 million to $788 million, while corporate tax expense rose $208 million to $4,699 million.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $1,563 million to $25,586 million. Driven by an $92 billion (8%) growth in average interest earning assets to $1,246 billion, partly offset by a 3 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.05%. Excluding liquid assets, NIM was stable.

Other operating income increased $196 million to $4,638 million. Commissions rose $135 million to $2,234 million; lending fees increased $12 million to $924 million; funds management income rose $12 million to $134 million; other income increased $46 million to $156 million; trading income decreased $9 million to $1,190 million.

Underlying operating expenses increased $719 million to $13,585 million. Staff expenses rose $288 million to $8,258 million; IT services expenses increased $393 million to $2,782 million; other expenses rose $57 million to $1,607 million; occupancy and equipment expenses decreased $19 million to $938 million.
Notable/restructuring items increased by $40 million to $170 million in FY26 compared to $130 million in FY25, representing a negative contribution to earnings.

Loan impairment expense increased $62 million to $788 million. Retail Banking Services saw an increase of $106 million to $378 million; Business Banking decreased $45 million to $310 million; NZ increased $11 million to $66 million; IB&M decreased $16 million to $33 million.
Corporate tax expense increased $208 million to $4,699 million. The effective tax rate decreased 50 basis points to 30.0%, primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses.

notable_items: Restructuring and notable items increased $40 million to $170 million.
limitations: Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
